newsitem.title: GERMANY: Air India drops loss-making Europe-India freighter.
newsitem.headline: Air India drops loss-making Europe-India freighter.

text.p: Air India has cancelled its four-times-weekly Brussels to India freighter service due to high losses, the airline's cargo sales manager Germany, Ruediger Brasche, told Reuters in an interview.
He said the service was not viable as a result of heavy fuel costs and falling cargo rates.
Brasche said Air India ended the service, which offered a total of 150 tonnes weekly capacity to Mumbai (Bombay), Delhi, Madras, Calcutta and Bangalore, on August 24.
The service was operated twice-a-week with an Iluyshin-76, with a capacity of up to 35 tonnes, and twice-weekly with a McDonnell Douglas DC-8F, with space for 40 tonnes.
"We made losses with the freighter which could not be tolerated any more," Brasche said.
In particular, the Iluyshin was very expensive, requiring up to two litres of fuel per kilo of cargo carried, he pointed out.
The recent fall in ex-India air cargo rates from 60-70 rupees per kilo to 40 rupees also damaged the route's viability, he said.
Brasche added: "We have no plans to resume freighter operations in the short-term."
